To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human hippocampus is involved in episodic memory and the hippocampus indexes the neocorti cal regions that represent an episode.
1) the hippocampus indexes the pattern of neoco- rtical activity that is associated with a behavioral episode and 2) this index serves as the basis for episodic memory retrieval.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural substrates of episodic memory and the mechanisms by which information is encoded, stored, and retrieved from the human brain.
the neural basis of memory and its relationship to other cognitive functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the hippocampal indexing theory has aged very well, that its core ideas are still valid and that the theory has provided a conceptual and empirical framework for much of what is currently known about episodic memory.
the indexing theory is correct in its basic assumptions and that the hippocampus does indeed serve as an index for episodic memory.
the hippocampus, and the medial temporal lobe more generally, plays an essential role in the formation of new memories, and is necessary for the recollection of episodic memories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to show that the hippocampus is a pattern recognition device that can be used to recognize the patterns of activity in the sensory and motor cortices and to use those patterns to retrieve the episodic memory associated with them.
the hippocampus is a pattern completion device, and it is this function of the hippocampus that makes episodic memory possible.
indexing theory was a very good idea.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the indexing theory has stood the test of time.
indexing theory has been validated in the last 20 years by a wide range of data and has been adopted as the conceptual basis for a number of other theories of memory.
indexing theory is alive and well.
